title: Algebraic structure in holographic tensor networks
authors: Abhisek Sahu, Jeremy van der Heijden, Mark Van Raamsdonk, Rana Zibakhsh
abstract: In a previous work 2511.21852, we explored the hypothesis that in general theories of quantum gravity, spacetime regions known as generalized entanglement wedges (introduced by Bousso and Penington) have an associated subalgebra of observables in a semiclassical limit. We defined an entropy associated with these subalgebras that obeys the same monotonicity and strong subadditivity properties as the generalized gravitational entropy of generalized entanglement wedges. Here, we test aspects of these ideas making use of tensor network toy models for holography. In this context, the analog of a generalized entanglement wedge is a region for which no region containing it has a smaller number of boundary legs. In the limit of large bond dimension (analogous to the semiclassical limit), we argue that each such region has a canonically associated subalgebra of the full algebra of observables on the boundary Hilbert space, as well as a family of unitarily related von Neumann factor subalgebras. We investigate in detail how various algebraic operations on these subalgebras (e.g. their intersections, joins, and commutants) are related to corresponding geometrical operations on the tensor network regions. We study to what extent the monotonicity and strong subadditivity properties of generalized entropy for generalized entanglement wedges follow from properties of our algebraic entropy. We also introduce an alternative entropic quantity $S(ω|| ω\circ E_{\mathcal{A}'})$ associated with a subalgebra $\mathcal{A}$ that also obeys monotonicity and strong subadditivity properties with suitable conditions. Finally, we explain how to define a type $II_1$ von Neumann algebra based on an infinite family of random tensor networks with increasing bond dimension such that the regions corresponding to generalized entanglement wedges can be associated with exact subalgebras of this full algebra.
summary: This work explores the deep connection between geometry and algebra in the context of quantum gravity holography using tensor network models. It shows that regions analogous to entanglement wedges correspond to specific subalgebras of observables. By analyzing how algebraic operations mirror geometric ones, the paper provides a concrete, computable test for fundamental principles like strong subadditivity in quantum gravity theories.
main_problem: The paper investigates the algebraic structure associated with generalized entanglement wedges in quantum gravity, using tensor network models to test fundamental properties like monotonicity and strong subadditivity.
main_result: The authors establish a correspondence between extremal geometric regions in the tensor network model and canonically associated von Neumann factor subalgebras of the observable algebra in the semiclassical limit.
method: The study employs tensor network toy models, analyzing algebraic operations (intersections, joins) on derived subalgebras and comparing the resulting algebraic entropy properties to geometric expectations.
model_or_system: The system is holographic, modeled by random tensor networks whose boundary Hilbert space and observable algebra are analyzed. The core analogy is mapping generalized entanglement wedges (GWs) to specific subalgebras.
key_observables: Generalized entropy ($S_{	ext{gen}}$), algebraic entropy ($S_{	ext{alg}}$), and the structure of associated von Neumann factor subalgebras ($\mathcal{M}_A$).
important_parameters: Large bond dimension (semiclassical limit), bond dimension $D$, and the structure of the tensor network graph.
main_assumptions: The analysis heavily relies on assuming isometric tensor networks and that the resulting subalgebras are von Neumann factors to simplify the algebraic investigation.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the correspondence between GWs and subalgebras, then detailing how algebraic operations map to geometric operations, and finally introducing alternative entropic quantities and methods to define the full Type II1 von Neumann algebra.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting geometric concepts from quantum gravity (entanglement wedges) to algebraic structures derived from tensor networks provides a powerful, computable tool for understanding holographic duality.
